summary: Canary coordinator deadlock during multi-region traffic shift causing routing stall and session anchoring failures
description: Issue summary: During a cross-region canary traffic shift for customer CartoAI (dedicated), the canary-coordinator entered a deadlocked state, causing routing decisions to stall and session anchoring to fail intermittently. Impact: ~35% of CartoAI requests in us-east experienced 5-10s extra latency and session-level fallback to default model, causing degraded quality. Some sessions lost their pinned model, resulting in surprising model swaps. Environment: production clusters in us-east and eu-west; dedicated capacity pool carto-dedicated-1 using redwood-open-7b-v2 as primary and redwood-opt-3b as fallback. Observed behavior: coordinator stopped progressing canary state machine after step adjust-weight, leaving a partial routing snapshot; edge proxies re-evaluated pins and evicted session-affinity tokens then routed to fallback variants. Expected behavior: coordinator completes weight adjustment, routing-service reconciles session pins without evictions, no deadlock and graceful fallback if necessary.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create multi-region canary with weight shift 0->20% in eu-west then 0->30% in us-east
2) Target a dedicated capacity pool with mixed model variants and session affinity enabled
3) Trigger concurrent canary weight adjustments (overlap window 15s) and observe coordinator logs
4) Monitor routing-service metrics and session-affinity counters during overlap

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: overlapping weight adjustments led to coordinator lock contention on per-tenant routing snapshot file
We observed a rare path in coordinator where ack from remote region times out but transaction lock remains held, preventing completion
Routing-service logs show reconciliation loop increased affinity eviction rate by 3x during the stall
No hardware failures detected; dedicated pool healthy, GPU utilization normal
Edge proxies treated stale snapshot as authoritative and cleared local TTLs leading to session pin loss
customer_impact_summary: CartoAI reported spike in response latency and quality regressions for target users on the canary cohort; business impact medium-high for customer (dedicated contract).
actions_taken: Scaled up coordinator replicas in us-east to reduce lock contention
Applied emergency hotfix to coordinator to add a bounded retry and ensure lock release on ack timeout (temporary mitigation)
Pinned affected CartoAI routes back to previous model version and aborted remaining canary steps
Raised an internal incident in #incidents and paged on-call routing engineer
next_steps: Engineering: ship coordinator fix to master that converts the blocking per-tenant file lock to optimistic CAS with compensating transactions (PR referenced)
SRE: add probe to detect coordinator progress stalls and auto-bump replica count as temporary protective measure
Product/SE: communicate remediation and timeline to CartoAI CSM and provide expanded logs and RCA draft
Ops: schedule rolling redeploy of routing-service with stricter TTL invariants for session-affinity
comments: Sofia Martinez (Support): Customer reported elevated latency and model flips. Collected request IDs and initial logs.
Dmitri Kozlov (SRE): Confirmed coordinator stalled. Temporarily scaled replicas and performed hotfix. Need engineering review for permanent fix.

Anika Rao (Engineer): Investigating PR; root cause likely lock retention on ack timeout. Preparing non-blocking alternative. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/canary-coordinator/pull/198

resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation applied (replica scale and hotfix). Customer routes re-pinned to previous stable model. Engineering PR prepared to remove blocking locks and add observability for coordinator progress. Plan to release permanent fix in next patch cycle and run a controlled canary test with CartoAI. Follow-up: full RCA and postmortem to be posted to Confluence and shared with customer.
